archetype.name: Pocket Passer (intermediate attacker)
archetype.definition: A tall, big-armed passer who wins from the pocket by layering throws into the 10-to-19-yard window off a strong run game. This year his legs are a small part of his game.

report.headline: Lawrence's accuracy leap is real; the touchdown rate and the volume are the catch.
report.take:
For four seasons Trevor Lawrence has looked like a quarterback about to be very good, with the accuracy numbers to undercut it. His CPOE ranked 41st last year and 40th the year before, and his bad-throw rate sat between 14 and 20 percent. This season those numbers have moved. He is at +6.22 CPOE (8th of 47) and a 9.6% bad-throw rate (3rd of 38), a 4.3-point drop from last year. He is getting the ball out faster too, with time to throw down to 2.72 from 2.87. Together that produces 0.282 EPA per dropback, 7th in the league and far beyond anything in his career log. That isn't a hot month. It is seven games of cleaner ball placement.

The engine is the intermediate level. On 58 throws between 10 and 19 air yards he is at 0.713 EPA a play with a 65.5% success rate and +8.4 CPOE. His 10-plus-yard throws as a group have added 62.9 EPA, against 22.6 from everything shorter. Parker Washington (48 targets) and Jakobi Meyers (0.547 EPA per target) are the main beneficiaries. Liam Coen's offense sets it up: a run-neutral pass rate (-2 over expected), a rushing attack ranked 6th in EPA, and play-action from under center, where Lawrence is at 0.422 EPA a play. Defenses can't sit on the short stuff.

What the box score flatters is the touchdowns. His 8.6% TD rate ranks 3rd and paces to 41 scores. That rate leans on 10 red-zone touchdowns despite a 51.4% completion rate inside the 20, and on a 4-TD, 22-attempt deep sample. His career high is 29, set last year. What the box score undersells is how little he throws. At 28.3 attempts a game, with the league's 3rd-ranked defense setting up leads, he ranks only 15th in yards per game while ranking 5th in yards per attempt. The Week 8 rout of Indianapolis, with 14 attempts, shows the cost.

Going forward, the accuracy and the intermediate game look like a skill change, not luck, and should hold up. Touchdowns should drift toward roughly two a game. Volume stays capped as long as this defense keeps handing him leads. That defense is about to face a Baltimore offense on its third quarterback.

strengths.title: Accuracy jump with real roots
strengths.body: His CPOE is up 8.1 points on last season and his bad-throw rate is down to 3rd-best among charted passers. He has never been close to either mark before. It comes with a quicker release and a lower aggressiveness rate, so this looks like better processing rather than easy throws padding the numbers. Expect some give-back, but not a collapse.

strengths.title: Owns the intermediate window
strengths.body: The 10-to-19-yard level produces most of his value. He is at 0.713 EPA a play there with +8.4 CPOE. The run game and under-center play-action pull linebackers up and open those windows. With 58 attempts, this is a large enough sample to trust as his identity.

strengths.title: Turnovers back to league-normal
strengths.body: He ranked 58th or worse in interceptions in three of his five seasons. This year his 2.0% INT rate sits right around the league average of 2.3%. That matters more than it sounds for a passer who works the middle of the field this much.

concerns.title: Touchdown rate will regress
concerns.body: His 8.6% TD rate ranks 3rd, against a league average of 4.6%. It is propped up by 10 red-zone scores on only 51.4% completions inside the 20, plus a four-touchdown deep sample on 22 throws. The efficiency is real; this conversion rate on this volume is not. Expect the scoring to cool even if the yards per attempt hold.

concerns.title: Volume capped by his own defense
concerns.body: A top-3 defense and a run-leaning script keep him at 28.3 attempts a game. That is why a 5th-ranked yards-per-attempt passer sits 15th in yards per game. This is a product of his role rather than a flaw in his game, but it limits his ceiling in lopsided wins, as the 14-attempt Week 8 showed.

concerns.title: Tight-game and third-down wobble
concerns.body: In close fourth quarters he is at 0.082 EPA with -7 CPOE. Three of his four interceptions came on third down, which he faces with an average of 9 yards to go. The samples are small, 30 and 51 plays, so treat this as a hint rather than a pattern. Still, it is the one place the old inaccuracy shows up.

trend.note: His efficiency has barely moved: the last five games sit at 0.285 EPA per dropback against 0.282 for the season. Volume rose to 39 and 41 attempts in Weeks 5-6, then fell to 14 in the Indianapolis blowout. His CPOE has also slipped to +0.7 over the last three games, even as yards per attempt climbed.

nextGame.headline: Soft secondary, depleted Ravens offense: efficient day, modest volume.
nextGame.body:
Baltimore's defense ranks 18th in EPA and 17th against the pass. It is exposed exactly where Lawrence is strongest. It allows 0.799 EPA on deep throws (27th), and lead receivers have been at 0.77 EPA per target against it, dead last. Parker Washington's role makes that a direct line for this offense. The one tough spot is the tight end: TE1s are held to -0.07 EPA a play (5th), so Brenton Strange may be quieter. Baltimore's 8th-ranked hit rate means he will take some contact, and his 24.4% pressure-to-sack rate leaves room for a sack or two.

Availability tilts this heavily. Lamar Jackson is headed for thumb surgery and injured reserve, Tyler Huntley probably won't play, and Joe Fagnano is limited with an ankle. That is why Jacksonville is laying 8.5 points on the road at -440. Safety Jaylinn Hawkins (81% of snaps) is out, which thins the deep coverage further. Linebacker Roquan Smith and edge rusher Trey Hendrickson are questionable. On Lawrence's side, Meyers (hamstring), Tuten (ankle, sat Monday's walkthrough) and left guard Ezra Cleveland (knee) are all questionable on a four-day turnaround. Losing Meyers and Tuten would take away two of his most efficient targets. The flip side of a big lead is another run-heavy second half, which caps his attempts.

keyMatchups.title: Washington against a leaky WR1 coverage
keyMatchups.body: Baltimore has allowed the most EPA per target in the league to opposing lead receivers. Washington leads Jacksonville in targets and is producing 0.452 EPA per target. This is the best route to an efficient first half.

keyMatchups.title: Shots against a thin safety group
keyMatchups.body: With Hawkins out and Baltimore 27th against deep throws, Lawrence's deep ball should have chances. It runs at 0.981 EPA a play on a small 22-attempt sample. One or two hits could carry the stat line even on low volume.

keyMatchups.title: Script risk from Baltimore's QB crisis
keyMatchups.body: Baltimore's likely third-string quarterback, plus a Jaguars defense ranked 3rd, points toward an early lead. This team has protected leads by running before. When ahead by 9 or more, Lawrence has thrown only 33 times all season.

nextGame.watch: Whether Meyers and Tuten play on the short week. Without them, the intermediate game runs almost entirely through Washington and Strange, against a defense that holds tight ends down.

restOfSeason.body:
The accuracy gains and the intermediate-level production rest on cleaner mechanics and a faster release, and they have held for seven games. That should keep him in the top tier in yards per attempt and EPA per dropback. What should cool is the scoring. A red-zone conversion rate built on sub-52% completions and a small, explosive deep sample won't keep producing 2.4 touchdowns a game. Expect something closer to 1.7 to 2.3.

Volume is the limiting factor. With an elite defense and a run game that works, he is a 27-to-32-attempt passer unless injuries or a better opponent force more dropbacks. The 39- and 41-attempt games against Philadelphia and Houston show his upside when games stay close; Indianapolis shows the low end. Forecast him at roughly 225 to 270 passing yards a game, with few rushing yards from a role that has moved away from his legs.
swingFactors: Health of Meyers and Tuten, his most efficient targets
How often the defense creates blowouts that shrink his volume
Whether red-zone touchdown conversion holds or reverts

confidence.note: Seven games is enough to trust the accuracy shift, which shows up across several stats. TD rate and deep splits rest on small samples.
